evidence: Select on a two-speed axle: if (two_speed_axle_enable_cal != 0) it loads rear_axle_ratio_high_cal and then rear_axle_ratio_low_cal when (switch_input_state_bits[3] & 0x80) == 0 (switch 31 clear); with the enable 0 it stores nothing, so rear_axle_ratio keeps the start-up HIGH value of 0x42770. The output shaft consumers use the LOW record in that single-speed case instead (cm848_calculateVehicleSpeedFromOutputShaft: (two_speed_axle_enable_cal == 0) || ((switch_input_state_bits[3] & 0x80) == 0) -> protection_trim_divisor_working). Dump (word): rear_axle_ratio, rear_axle_ratio_low_cal and rear_axle_ratio_high_cal are all 453, two_speed_axle_enable_cal is 0.
plate_comment: Selects the rear axle ratio in use for a two-speed axle: rear_axle_ratio (e2m 117D +30 Rear_Axle_Ratio, 1/128 per count) is set from rear_axle_ratio_high_cal (EEPROM 0xb2, e2m 1180 +C Rear_Axle_Ratio_High) and, while switch 31 (switch_input_state_bits[3] bit 0x80) is clear, from rear_axle_ratio_low_cal (EEPROM 0xac, e2m 1180 +6 Rear_Axle_Ratio_Low). The stores run only when two_speed_axle_enable_cal is nonzero; with it 0 the word keeps the start-up value that 0x42770 loads from the HIGH record, whereas cm848_calculateVehicleSpeedFromOutputShaft and cm848_calculateDrivetrainRatioFromVehicleSpeed use the LOW record in that single-speed case. Called every pass of cm848_periodicTaskSet_auxiliaryControl. Inputs: two_speed_axle_enable_cal, switch 31, the two ratio records. Output: rear_axle_ratio (read by cm848_processGovernorSpeedSetpoint, cm848_calculateRiseLimitedVehicleSpeed and cm848_calculateCruisePidRateGainScale). 453 = 3.54 in the dump for all three words; two_speed_axle_enable_cal is 0 there.

evidence: The whole body is one store, rear_axle_ratio = rear_axle_ratio_high_cal; (the HIGH record, EEPROM 0xb2, e2m 1180 +C). Its only caller is the boot list of cm848_applicationMain, right before the divisor calculation 0x5268e8, so it runs once at start-up. The periodic select 0x4272c stores nothing while two_speed_axle_enable_cal is 0, so this value stays in use on a single-speed axle. Dump (word): 453.
plate_comment: Start-up initializer of the rear axle ratio in use: rear_axle_ratio (e2m 117D +30 Rear_Axle_Ratio, 1/128 per count) = rear_axle_ratio_high_cal (EEPROM 0xb2, e2m 1180 +C Rear_Axle_Ratio_High). Called once from the boot list of cm848_applicationMain, just before the divisor calculation 0x5268e8. The value stays in use on a single-speed axle (two_speed_axle_enable_cal = 0: the periodic select 0x4272c then stores nothing) and is the start value on a two-speed axle, where the periodic select replaces it with rear_axle_ratio_low_cal while switch 31 is clear. 453 = 3.54 in the dump.

evidence: protection_trim_divisor_working = rear_axle_ratio_low_cal * protection_timing_period_cal and protection_trim_divisor_cal = rear_axle_ratio_high_cal * protection_timing_period_cal; protection_timing_period_cal (0x3fee7a) is e2m 132C +0 Tire_Size (tire revolutions per mile). The only reader of the two products is cm848_calculateVehicleSpeedFromOutputShaft: output_shaft_speed_current x 0x3c000 / divisor, and 0x3c000 = 256 x 60 x 128 / 8 (1/256 mph from 1/8 rpm with the ratio in 1/128), so they are divisors, not trims. Called once from the boot list of cm848_applicationMain after the rear axle ratio initializer. Dump: Tire_Size word 251 (the e2m range is 300-725; not interpreted), both divisors dword 113703 = 453 x 251.
plate_comment: Start-up calculation of the output shaft speed to vehicle speed divisors: protection_trim_divisor_working (0x3fd062) = rear_axle_ratio_low_cal x protection_timing_period_cal and protection_trim_divisor_cal (0x3fd066) = rear_axle_ratio_high_cal x protection_timing_period_cal, one dword each. The ratio words are e2m 1180 +6 / +C (1/128 per count); protection_timing_period_cal (EEPROM mirror 0x3fee7a) is e2m 132C +0 Tire_Size, the number of tire revolutions per mile (the e2m range is 300-725; 251 in the dump). cm848_calculateVehicleSpeedFromOutputShaft divides output_shaft_speed_current (1/8 rpm) x 0x3c000 (= 256 x 60 x 128 / 8) by the _cal divisor when two_speed_axle_enable_cal is on and switch 31 is set, else by the _working one, which gives vehicle speed in 1/256 mph. Called once from the boot list of cm848_applicationMain, after the rear axle ratio initializer 0x42770. 113703 = 453 x 251 for both in the dump.

evidence: Estimate + filter + settle state of the drivetrain ratio (engine speed over vehicle or output shaft speed x 2048): for the drivetrain types without a J1939 speed it computes drivetrain_ratio_raw = vehicle_speed_sensor_period x drivetrain_ratio_period_scale_cal x 16 / drivetrain_ratio_engine_period_average (0x7ffd when it cannot be computed), then exponentialMovingAverage((uint)drivetrain_ratio_raw, &engine_temperature_protection_filter_state) -> drivetrain_ratio, then the limit / tolerance check, the out-of-gear timers that clear drivetrain_ratio_unsettled_flag, governor_j1939_bypass_flag 1 / 2 / 3 against the top gear thresholds and the stable-divisor save. The J1939 types get their raw ratio elsewhere (cm848_calculateDrivetrainRatioFromVehicleSpeed) and only pass through the filter here, so update covers every path; estimate (the other proposal) covers one. Limit compare: (drivetrain_ratio_minimum_limit < uVar4) && (uVar4 < DAT_0005c932) with uVar4 = drivetrain_ratio_raw. Caller: cm848_periodicTaskSet_outputs.
plate_comment: Drivetrain ratio update, one pass of cm848_periodicTaskSet_outputs (skipped while drivetrain_type is DRIVETRAIN_STANDALONE). The ratio is engine speed over vehicle (or output shaft) speed x 2048. While vehicle_speed is below vehicle_speed_minimum or the engine is stopped it reseeds drivetrain_ratio_raw, drivetrain_ratio, fuel_flow_rpm_divisor, fuel_flow_rpm_divisor_saved and the filter accumulator with drivetrain_ratio_default and sets drivetrain_ratio_unsettled_flag. Otherwise, on the drivetrain types without a J1939 speed, it computes drivetrain_ratio_raw = vehicle_speed_sensor_period x drivetrain_ratio_period_scale_cal (e2m 1195 +2 GR_Constant) x 16 / drivetrain_ratio_engine_period_average (0x7ffd = not computable); the J1939 types get it elsewhere. It low-pass filters drivetrain_ratio_raw into drivetrain_ratio (the settled or the out-of-gear filter coefficient), checks it against the minimum / maximum limits and tolerances (in window: fuel_flow_rpm_divisor = drivetrain_ratio; outside: fuel_flow_divisor_invalid_flag = 1, the raw ratio is clamped and drivetrain_ratio_change_settle_counter is reloaded) and runs the out-of-gear timers (drivetrain_ratio_decoupled_hold_counter, drivetrain_ratio_unsettled_release_timer; e2m 106C +6 / +8) that clear drivetrain_ratio_unsettled_flag (e2m 117D +E Out_Of_Gear) only when all are 0. It also publishes governor_bypass_threshold_low / _high (from top_gear_ratio_cal, e2m 1185 +A), sets governor_j1939_bypass_flag to 1 / 2 / 3 as drivetrain_ratio is below the low / below the high / above the high threshold, and commits fuel_flow_rpm_divisor_saved once the divisor is stable and final_fueling is above its threshold.

evidence: The whole body is if (vehicle_speed_unfiltered != 0) { ecm_power_down_delay_request_flag = 1; } (e2m 117D +4C Powerdown_Delay_Request '[SDDYFG] The ECM will not powerdown until this is inactive'). cm848_updateEngineState starts the delayed power-down only while (ecm_power_down_timer != 0 && ecm_power_down_delay_request_flag == 0) and clears the flag at the end of every SHUTDOWN pass. No fuel demand is involved. Caller: cm848_periodicTaskSet_sensorProcessing. Dump (word): the flag and vehicle_speed_unfiltered are both 0 (no speed sensor wired).
plate_comment: Requests a delay of the ECM power-down while the vehicle is moving: sets ecm_power_down_delay_request_flag (e2m 117D +4C Powerdown_Delay_Request, '[SDDYFG] The ECM will not powerdown until this is inactive') to 1 when vehicle_speed_unfiltered (1/256 mph, from the speed sensor or the J1939 output shaft speed) is nonzero, and never clears it. cm848_updateEngineState starts the delayed power-down in SHUTDOWN only while the flag is 0 and clears it at the end of every SHUTDOWN pass. Runs every pass of cm848_periodicTaskSet_sensorProcessing. On this truck the speed reads 0 (no speed sensor wired), so the flag is never set (0 in the dump).

evidence: converter_clutch_rationality_ratio_delta_sum = saturate16((short)converter_clutch_rationality_ratio_delta_sum + (short)protection_pid_error_term) (clamps 0x8000 / 0x7fff): a running sum of the ratio deltas of the P1740 converter clutch rationality test (fault 319 -> ROM slot table 0x5985a -> obd_dtc_code_table = P1740), e2m 8C34 +9 TCC_Rationality_Sum_Ratio_Delta; no setpoint, gain or integrator term. Called by cm848_monitorConverterClutchAndOverdrivePerformance right after the delta function 0x51ba6c, at the start of an engagement and on each timed step.
plate_comment: Accumulates the converter clutch rationality ratio delta: converter_clutch_rationality_ratio_delta_sum (e2m 8C34 +9 TCC_Rationality_Sum_Ratio_Delta, signed word, 1/256) = signed 16-bit saturating sum of itself and protection_pid_error_term (the ratio delta that 0x51ba6c just calculated); it clamps at -32768 / 32767. Called by cm848_monitorConverterClutchAndOverdrivePerformance (the P1740 converter clutch / overdrive performance monitor) right after each ratio delta, at the start of an engagement and on each timed step. The monitor judges the sum against protection_pid_integrator_threshold (e2m 8C33 +7 TCC_Rationality_Min_Ratio_Delta) when the rationality timer reaches its limit. It is a plain running sum, not a PID integrator. 0 in the dump.

evidence: protection_pid_error_term = saturate16(protection_pid_rpm_setpoint_prev - converter_clutch_rationality_ratio): the previous sample of the engine speed to output speed ratio (e2m 8C34 +7 TCC_Rationality_Ratio) minus the new one; the caller stores the new sample into protection_pid_rpm_setpoint_prev afterwards. No setpoint or gain is involved, so it is not a PID error. Caller: cm848_monitorConverterClutchAndOverdrivePerformance (P1740: fault 319 -> ROM slot table 0x5985a -> obd_dtc_code_table), two calls, each followed by 0x51ba1c.
plate_comment: Calculates the converter clutch rationality ratio delta: protection_pid_error_term = saturate16(protection_pid_rpm_setpoint_prev - converter_clutch_rationality_ratio), i.e. the previous sample of the engine speed to transmission output speed ratio minus the new sample (converter_clutch_rationality_ratio, e2m 8C34 +7 TCC_Rationality_Ratio, 1/256), clamped to -32768..32767. Called by cm848_monitorConverterClutchAndOverdrivePerformance (the P1740 monitor) after each new ratio sample and followed by the sum update 0x51ba1c; the monitor then stores the new sample into protection_pid_rpm_setpoint_prev. Not a PID error: no setpoint or gain is involved. 0 in the dump.

evidence: Channel 1 is the cam signal: e2m 8194 +56 PMA_Edge_Type 'Capture edge for cam signal' is the byte crank_mios_channel1_config_cal that mpc555_resetEngineTimingAccumulators ORs into tpu_a_ch1_param2.PARAM0 (PMM_Edge_Type 8194 +57 'crank signal' is channel 0's). This handler reloads backup_pulse_period_countdown (819B +A Backup_Lost_Counter) from crank_sync_timing_scale_working, stores the 24-bit period in the ring (&crank_period_capture_array)[crank_period_capture_index] (819B +4E Pulse_Period_Table_Backup, +3E Next_Table_Position_Backup) and sums it into crank_tooth_period_raw (+6 Average_Pulse_Period_Backup), reads crank_period_computed = TPUA_CH3_PARAM2 & 0xff (819B +E Cam_2_Crank_Tooth_Number) against crank_tooth_pattern_table (Cam_2_Crank_Position_Array) and writes engine_crank_state_t.crank_state, which is e2m 819C +2 Cam_Sync_State (only 0 / 1 / 4 = NO / LOST / HAVE here; the channel 0 handler walks run_state, 819C +6 Crank_Sync_State, through 2 / 3 = START / PRELIM). crank_event_timebase_a (819B +72 Cam_Have_Sync_Time) is stored when crank_state is 4. HSRR1 = 1 is a host service request on channel 0 (bits 1:0): mpc555_resetEngineTimingAccumulators initializes channel 0 with HSRR1 = 3 and channel 1 with 0xc.
plate_comment: TPU-A channel 1 interrupt handler - reached via tpu_a_channel_interrupt_handler_table (mpc555_tpuAInterruptDispatcher 0x55de4) - no direct caller in the decompile. Channel 1 is the cam signal input (the TPU PMA function: e2m 8194 +56 PMA_Edge_Type 'Capture edge for cam signal' is crank_mios_channel1_config_cal, which goes into tpu_a_ch1_param2.PARAM0), so this is the backup engine speed path, not the crank. Per cam pulse it reloads backup_pulse_period_countdown (e2m 819B +A Backup_Lost_Counter) from crank_sync_timing_scale_working; with a nonzero tooth count it stores the 24-bit period of tpu_a_ch1_param2 into the ring crank_period_capture_array (819B +4E Pulse_Period_Table_Backup, index crank_period_capture_index = +3E Next_Table_Position_Backup) and sums it into crank_tooth_period_raw (+6 Average_Pulse_Period_Backup) and engine_rpm_state_t.crank_tooth_period_sum / _sample_count (the backup accumulator +24 and counter +2A). It runs the cam sync state engine_crank_state_t.crank_state (e2m 819C +2 Cam_Sync_State; here 0 NO / 1 LOST / 4 HAVE, driven by the channel status byte), the pattern machine from tpu_a_ch1_param2: start_counter (819C +0 Cam_Sync_Error_Count) rises while LOST above speed_setpoint_minimum and falls while HAVE, and crank_event_timebase_a (819B +72 Cam_Have_Sync_Time) is stored once at HAVE. It compares the crank tooth number of the cam pulse (crank_period_computed from TPUA_CH3_PARAM2, 819B +E Cam_2_Crank_Tooth_Number) with crank_tooth_pattern_table (Cam_2_Crank_Position_Array, 2 x cam_wheel_pulse_count entries), counts matches in crank_tooth_count_a / crank_sync_period_counter and mismatches in crank_sync_timeout_count (819B +10 Cam_Crank_Mismatch_Count), and requests a TPU host service (tpu_a_mcr.HSRR1 = 1) with crank_resync_time_ticks / crank_tbl_event_counter when the crank bank is out of phase, then dispatches the run state handlers and the injection timing (engine_injectionTiming_crankSyncDispatch, cm848_enterSpeedLimpHome).

evidence: Single caller: the boot list of cm848_applicationMain, between cm848_sensor_diagnostic_flag_update and cm848_initializeFuelPressureDiagnosticState / cm848_initializeFuelPressureSetpointState, so it is one of the start-up initializers, not an engine sync reset. It zeroes fuel_metering_command and fuel_pressure_governor_demand, stores FUEL_PRESSURE_GOVERNOR_OPEN_LOOP_START (the quote), clears the integrator / derivative states, sets the 17 lookup cache words engine_sync_init_state_a..q to 2, points seven EMA records at their coefficients (e.g. fuel_pressure_sensor_filter.coefficient = &fuel_pressure_sensor_filter_coefficient) and presets the coil resistance estimate (fuel_metering_coil_temperature = sensor_readings_t_0040baf2.coolant_temp). The old plate is kept in full, including the 0x3fb676 quirk (the fourth store pair repeats 0x3fb66e).
plate_comment: Initializes (resets) the fuel pressure governor / fuel metering state (cm848_calculateFuelMeteringCommand): command, demand, governor mode 1, counters, the table interpolation states and filters. Of the four Q16.16 PID states it clears fuel_pressure_governor_integrator, fuel_metering_feedback_trim_integrator (twice) and fuel_pressure_governor_derivative_filter; fuel_metering_base_command_derivative_filter (0x3fb676) is never cleared because the fourth store pair repeats 0x3fb66e. In detail: fuel_metering_command and fuel_pressure_governor_demand = 0, fuel_pressure_governor_mode and its saved copy = FUEL_PRESSURE_GOVERNOR_OPEN_LOOP_START, the start revolution / low pressure counters and the feed forward = 0, the 17 table lookup cache words engine_sync_init_state_a..q = 2, the EMA filter records of the fuel metering feedback / reference / command, the fuel pressure sensor, the accelerator feed forward and the two cam_sync_* speed filters = accumulator 0 with their coefficient pointers set, fuel_metering_command_filtered = 0, the coil resistance estimate (e2m 8019) preset from engine_sync_rpm_filter_initial_cal and the coolant temperature, and the engine_sync_* flags and governor_zero_speed_count = 0. Called once from the boot list of cm848_applicationMain, before the fuel pressure diagnostic and setpoint state initializers.

evidence: While cbd_enable_flag == 1 or misfire_monitor_speed_buffer_enable_flag == 1: uVar3 = (cylinder_balance_filtered_fueling - final_fueling) * cbd_fuel_demand_blend_scale_cal, iVar1 = uVar3 >> 13 (rounded toward 0), filtered = final_fueling + iVar1 clamped to 0..0x1700. That is a first-order low-pass of final_fueling (e2m 1051 +0) into cylinder_balance_filtered_fueling (e2m 81B0 +0 CBD_Filtered_Fueling) with the previous value weighted blend / 8192; there is no throttle or load input. Caller: cm848_periodicTaskSet_controlLoop. The hpcr_ prefix stays (the cylinder balance code is hpcr_cbd*).
plate_comment: Cylinder balance fueling filter: while the cylinder balance code is enabled (cbd_enable_flag = 1) or the misfire monitor's speed buffer is enabled (misfire_monitor_speed_buffer_enable_flag = 1) it low-pass filters final_fueling (e2m 1051 +0 Final_Fueling) into cylinder_balance_filtered_fueling (e2m 81B0 +0 CBD_Filtered_Fueling): filtered = final_fueling + (previous filtered - final_fueling) x cbd_fuel_demand_blend_scale_cal / 8192, clamped to 0..5888 (0x1700). That word is the fueling axis of the cylinder balance tables and the zero-fuel test of hpcr_cbdCalculateCylinderTrims. Runs every pass of cm848_periodicTaskSet_controlLoop. There is no throttle or load input.

evidence: Sets injection_angle_sequence_state = 1 and injection_tpu_period_parameter_address = 2 (TPU-A channel 0 parameter 1 per its row comment), programs TPU-A channel 6 (CFSR2 field 0xf00 = 9, HSRR1 = 0x3000, CIER |= 0x40, TPUA_CH6_PARAM0 = 0x6002 = 0x6000 | that address) and stores injection_timing_tooth_separation_per_cylinder = injection_timing_tooth_count / cylinder_event_count_max. Callers: the boot list of cm848_applicationMain and cm848_updateEngineSpeedFromCrankSignal (after engine_rpm_measured has dropped to 0, following mpc555_resetEngineTimingAccumulators). The row comment of injection_timing_tooth_separation_per_cylinder already calls this function the scheduler initializer; channel 6 is the injection scheduling channel (engine_injectionAngle_tpuChannel6EventHandler). Nothing in it touches a sensor or a diagnostic flag.
plate_comment: Initializes the injection angle scheduler, the TPU-A channel 6 per-cylinder injection event channel (handled by engine_injectionAngle_tpuChannel6EventHandler): sets injection_angle_sequence_state (e2m 805E +0 HPCR_Wakeup_Processing_Status_N) to 1 and injection_tpu_period_parameter_address (805E +B HPCR_Period_Address) to 2 (the primary speed input, TPU-A channel 0 parameter 1 at 0x304102), sets up channel 6 (CFSR2 function field 9, host service request 3 in HSRR1, channel interrupt enable bit 0x40 in CIER, priority field of CPR1; TPUA_CH6_PARAM0 = 0x6002 = 0x6000 | the period address) and stores injection_timing_tooth_separation_per_cylinder (805E +C HPCR_Wakeup_Seperation_In_Increments) = injection_timing_tooth_count / cylinder_event_count_max (120 / 6 = 20). Called once from the boot list of cm848_applicationMain and again by cm848_updateEngineSpeedFromCrankSignal after engine_rpm_measured has dropped to 0, right after mpc555_resetEngineTimingAccumulators.

evidence: Compares sensor_readings_t.barometric_pressure with governor_integrator_bound_a (sensor_channel_filtered_output[77]) and governor_integrator_bound_b ([38]) using barometric_pressure_sensor_tolerance, boost_pressure_sensor_tolerance and oil_pressure_sensor_tolerance (e2m 165C Ambient_Air / Boost / Oil_Sensor_Tolerence; the pairing in the code puts [77] with the boost tolerance and [38] with the oil one). A sensor sets its mask (4 / 8 / 0x10 of fault_detected_bits_592_to_607, faults 594 / 595 / 596 = e2m 1036 +4A System_Error_Status_37, no DTC slot: fault 594 -> ROM slot table 0x5985a -> slot 170) only when it is more than own tolerance + the other's away from BOTH others, e.g. (uint)barometric_pressure_sensor_tolerance + (uint)boost_pressure_sensor_tolerance < (uVar1 & 0xffff) && ... + (uint)oil_pressure_sensor_tolerance < (uVar2 & 0xffff), and clears it (and the twin bit in j1939_tsc1_mode_shadow) otherwise. It runs once from cm848_processSensorDeviationOnKeyoff after the engine has been stopped for cold_start_sensor_deviation_delay_cal (e2m 165C +6 Pressure_Check_Delay_Time), so the name says which sensors and what the verdict is.
plate_comment: Pressure sensor agreement check (e2m 165C: Ambient_Air_Sensor_Tolerence, Boost_Sensor_Tolerence, Oil_Sensor_Tolerence, Pressure_Check_Delay_Time), run once by cm848_processSensorDeviationOnKeyoff after the engine has been stopped for cold_start_sensor_deviation_delay_cal while algorithm_enable_flags_6_cal bit 0x20 is set. It compares three pressure readings, sensor_readings_t.barometric_pressure, governor_integrator_bound_a (sensor_channel_filtered_output[77], paired with the boost tolerance) and governor_integrator_bound_b ([38], paired with the oil tolerance), using barometric_pressure_sensor_tolerance, boost_pressure_sensor_tolerance and oil_pressure_sensor_tolerance. A sensor is flagged when it differs from both of the other two by more than the sum of its own tolerance and the other sensor's tolerance: mask 4 / 8 / 0x10 of fault_detected_bits_592_to_607 (faults 594 / 595 / 596, e2m 1036 +4A System_Error_Status_37, no DTC) for the barometric / first / second sensor. A bit and the same bit of its registered twin j1939_tsc1_mode_shadow (0x3fea22) are cleared when that sensor agrees with at least one other; all three bits are cleared when one of the sensor circuit faults the check depends on is set (fault_detected_bits_16_to_31 0x200 / 0x400, fault_detected_bits_0_to_15 0x100 / 0x200 / 0x1000 / 0x2000). Outputs: those three flag bits.

evidence: The whole body is not_safe_to_program_flag = engine_state != ENGINE_STATE_STOPPED; (e2m 000D +0 SAFE2PRG / Safe_To_Program: 0 safe, 1 not safe); it reads and writes no fault and no key-off state. Caller: cm848_periodicTaskSet_auxiliaryControl, every pass. Readers: cm848_forceActivateDiagnosticSession (DIAG_NACK_PROTECTED), cm848_commitEepromMirrorToEeprom, j1939_writeDiagMemory, cm848_processPciDiagnosticRequest and cm848_lookupParameterIdAddress. Dump (byte): 0 with engine_state 1 (STOPPED).
plate_comment: Updates not_safe_to_program_flag (e2m 000D +0 SAFE2PRG / Safe_To_Program: 'Indicator to tools (0 = safe for program, 1 = not safe)'): 1 while engine_state is not ENGINE_STATE_STOPPED, else 0. Runs every pass of cm848_periodicTaskSet_auxiliaryControl. Input: engine_state. Output: not_safe_to_program_flag. While it is 1 the force-activate diagnostic service answers DIAG_NACK_PROTECTED, cm848_commitEepromMirrorToEeprom refuses, the diagnostic EEPROM writes (j1939_writeDiagMemory, the PCI write service) answer 7 unless diagnostic_session_state is INACTIVE, and cm848_lookupParameterIdAddress maps EEPROM parameter addresses to the RAM mirror. It handles no fault and no key-off event.

evidence: param_1 is a step code, not the e2m EOL_Mil_State coding (its 3 turns the lamp on): 0 clears diag_suppress_saved_flag and the override; 1 saves the override into diag_suppress_saved_flag, sets end_of_line_test_malfunction_indicator_lamp_flash_request_flag = 1 and clears the override; 2 restores it (the quote) and clears the flash request; 3 sets the saved flag and the override to 1 (lamp on; cm848_updateMilOnRequest forces the MIL request on while the override is 1). Called by cm848_runEndOfLineTestSequence, cm848_runEndOfLineMisfireTestStep, the cold start / deviation / battery voltage / bit check steps and cm848_initialization_group21_state_cont (step 3 when the failed-test power-down flag is 1). e2m 1226 +C EOL_Mil_State, +D EOL_Mil_Flash; 'MalfunctionIndicatorLamp' is spelled out because mil is not on the allow-list.
plate_comment: Controls the malfunction indicator lamp (MIL) override of the Chrysler in-plant end-of-line test. param_1 is a step code, not the e2m EOL_Mil_State coding: 0 = clear the saved override (diag_suppress_saved_flag) and the override; 1 = save the current override into diag_suppress_saved_flag, request the lamp flash (end_of_line_test_malfunction_indicator_lamp_flash_request_flag = 1) and clear the override while the step runs; 2 = restore the saved override and clear the flash request; 3 = lamp on: save 1, override = 1, no flash request. Outputs: end_of_line_test_malfunction_indicator_lamp_override_state (e2m 1226 +C EOL_Mil_State; cm848_updateMilOnRequest forces the MIL request on while it is 1) and the flash request (e2m 1226 +D EOL_Mil_Flash, sent in bit 5 of PCI TX[3] byte 1 by cm848_buildPciTransmitMessage3MilAndDtcDisplay while the field mode register is 5100). Called by the end-of-line test sequencer and its steps (cm848_runEndOfLineTestSequence, cm848_runEndOfLineMisfireTestStep and the cold start, deviation, battery voltage and bit check steps) and, with step 3, by cm848_initialization_group21_state_cont at start-up when the failed-test power-down flag (e2m 1981 +1 EOL_MIL_Powerdown_State) is 1.

evidence: Direction checks: mask 1 is set when 0x9ff < coolant_temp - warm_up_cycle_start_coolant_temperature (a RISE of about 40 degrees F, 1/64 degree per count); mask 2 when warm_up_cycle_minimum_coolant_temperature < coolant_temp (coolant ABOVE 8960 = 140 degrees F, e2m 11F9 +2 Warm_Up_Temp_Max). At 3 it adds 1 to fault_auto_clear_warm_up_cycle_count_cal (< 0x27 then +1, else 0) and calls fault_ring_buffer_auto_clear_emission; there is no overheat compare. e2m 1226 +9 Warm_Up_Cycle_Flag. Caller: cm848_mainLoopServiceMonitor. Dump (byte): flags 0.
plate_comment: OBD warm-up cycle monitor (e2m 1226 +9 Warm_Up_Cycle_Flag, '[DGWUCYFL] Indicates whether warm up cycle has occurred'; it makes no coolant overheat check). Sets bit 0 of warm_up_cycle_condition_flags when coolant_temp has risen more than 0x9ff (about 40 degrees F; 1/64 degree per count) above warm_up_cycle_start_coolant_temperature (the sample taken after the startup delay) and bit 1 when coolant_temp is above warm_up_cycle_minimum_coolant_temperature (e2m 11F9 +2 Warm_Up_Temp_Max, 8960 = 140 degrees F). With both set (3) a warm-up cycle has occurred: it stops evaluating, adds 1 to fault_auto_clear_warm_up_cycle_count_cal (counts 0..39, then 0) and calls fault_ring_buffer_auto_clear_emission, which clears the fault ring. Called by cm848_mainLoopServiceMonitor. 0 in the dump (engine off).

evidence: Loops i = 0..7 and adds 1 to each engine_start_count_since_fault_logged_cal[i] (word[8], e2m 138F +2 Number_Of_Starts_1..8 'Number of engine starts since most recent fault logged') while it is below 255. Its only caller cm848_auxiliaryControlTask calls it once, on the first pass after engine_state is RUNNING / ENGINE_BRAKE / OVERSPEED, behind the once-flag DAT_003fd22b (its only access in the decompile sets it to 1). Dump (word): all eight 255.
plate_comment: Increments the engine start counts since a fault was logged: each of the eight words of engine_start_count_since_fault_logged_cal (EEPROM 0x194c, e2m 138F +2 Number_Of_Starts_1..8: starts since the 1st..8th most recent fault was logged; index 0 = newest, parallel to protection_event_spn_history) gets +1 while it is below 255. Called once per engine start by cm848_auxiliaryControlTask, on the first pass after engine_state is RUNNING, ENGINE_BRAKE or OVERSPEED, behind the once-flag DAT_003fd22b and fault_aging_triggered_flag = 0. 255 in all eight words in the dump.

evidence: for (i = param_1; i < 7; i++) engine_start_count_since_fault_logged_cal[i] = [i + 1]: every older entry moves one slot toward index 0 and closes the gap at param_1 (index 7 keeps its value). Its only caller fault_clearFromRing finds the cleared fault's code in protection_event_spn_history, calls this with that index and then closes the code list the same way ([i] = [i + 1], last = 0). The opposite direction of 0x533b94 ([i] = [i - 1]); 'shift in' named neither, so the name says remove.
plate_comment: Removes one entry from the engine start counts since a fault was logged (engine_start_count_since_fault_logged_cal, word[8], e2m 138F +2 Number_Of_Starts_1..8): for i = param_1 .. 6 it copies count[i] = count[i + 1], so every older entry moves one slot toward index 0 and closes the gap (index 7 keeps its value). Called by fault_clearFromRing with the index of a cleared fault's code in protection_event_spn_history, which fault_clearFromRing then closes the same way. Opposite direction of 0x533b94, which opens index 0 for a new fault.

evidence: for (i = 7; i != 0; i--) count[i] = *(word *)(i * 2 + 0x3fedcc), and 0x3fedcc + 2 i is count[i - 1] (the array starts at 0x3fedce): every entry ages one slot toward index 7 and the oldest (index 7) is dropped, which opens index 0. Its only caller cm848_latchNewlyActiveFault runs it on the first activation of a fault, right after shifting protection_event_spn_history the same way and writing the new code at index 0, then sets count[0] = 0. The opposite direction of 0x533b5c ([i] = [i + 1]).
plate_comment: Opens index 0 of the engine start counts since a fault was logged (engine_start_count_since_fault_logged_cal, word[8], e2m 138F +2 Number_Of_Starts_1..8): for i = 7 down to 1 it copies count[i] = count[i - 1] (read at 0x3fedcc + 2 i), so every entry ages one slot toward index 7 and the oldest (index 7) is dropped. Called by cm848_latchNewlyActiveFault when a fault latches for the first time, right after it has shifted protection_event_spn_history the same way and written the new code at index 0; the caller then sets count[0] = 0. Opposite direction of 0x533b5c, which closes a gap.

evidence: The sums feed the DRB '% OF TIME @ x LOAD' words: percent_time_at_load_cal[n] = (sum of the 8 fine counters of load band n) x 0x6400 / load_histogram_total_sample_count_cal (25600 = 100 percent); the 82 dwords from 0x3fde4e sum to the total in the dump (3203448 = dword at 0x3fde48). e2m: DC_Mon_Enable 106B +26 bit 0x0008 (the lhz mask 8 on algorithm_enable_flags_18_cal), DC_Mon_Load_Factor 111F +0, DC_Mon_Operating_Region 111F +2 (DAT_0040a64a, 81 in the dump), DC_Mon_Map_Reset 111F +3, DC_Mon_Low / High_Cutoff_RPM 111C, axes 111D / 111E (ROM 0x5c2c0 / 0x5c2d4), DC_Mon_Long_Map_Total 1122 +4. The sibling rows split between duty_cycle_monitor_* (the e2m DC_Mon records) and load_histogram_* (the EEPROM data), so the name carries both: it updates the monitor and fills the histogram. Cutoffs: current_rpm < duty_cycle_monitor_low_cutoff_engine_speed -> the maximum fueling is looked up at the low cutoff, current_rpm not below DAT_0005c2bc (the high cutoff) -> at the high cutoff. e2m 1125 DC_Mon_Long_Term_Map resolves to 0x3fde4c, 2 bytes before the counters the code uses (drift). Caller: cm848_periodicTaskSet_outputs2.
plate_comment: Duty cycle monitor load histogram (e2m group DC_Mon; enable 106B +26 DC_Mon_Enable = bit 3 of algorithm_enable_flags_18_cal), one sample per call of cm848_periodicTaskSet_outputs2 (1 count = 0.1 s in the e2m). While the monitor is enabled and the engine is not stopped: when load_histogram_total_sample_count_cal is 0 it first stores engine_hour_meter in load_histogram_start_engine_hours_cal; fuel_demand_histogram_load_ratio = (final_fueling - fuel_demand_base_offset) x 10000 / (the maximum fueling at the engine speed, from cm848_lookupChiMaximumFuelAtSpeed with the speed limited by the e2m 111C DC_Mon_Low / High_Cutoff_RPM, minus fuel_demand_base_offset), clamped at 13000 and copied to duty_cycle_monitor_load_factor (e2m 111F +0 DC_Mon_Load_Factor, 0.01 percent; 0 when the ratio is negative); the engine speed is binned against the 8 breakpoints of e2m 111D DC_Mon_RPM_Axis (ROM 0x5c2c0) and the load against the 10 of 111E DC_Mon_Load_Axis (0x5c2d4) into one of 80 fine counters, a negative load into counter 81 or 82, and the counter number is stored in DAT_0040a64a (e2m 111F +2 DC_Mon_Operating_Region); that fine counter and load_histogram_total_sample_count_cal (e2m 1122 +4 DC_Mon_Long_Map_Total, up to 3,600,000,000 = 100,000 h) get +1; percent_time_at_load_cal[0..9] (25600 = 100 percent, the DRB '% OF TIME @ x LOAD' words) are recomputed as each load band's 8 counters x 25600 / total, plus the two out-of-range percentages in 0x3fdfac / 0x3fdfae. The counters are the 82 dwords from 0x3fde4e (their sum equals the total in the dump, 3203448; e2m 1125 DC_Mon_Long_Term_Map resolves 2 bytes earlier, to 0x3fde4c). When the monitor is off or the engine is stopped it only acts on duty_cycle_monitor_map_reset_pending_flag (e2m 111F +3 DC_Mon_Map_Reset): it zeroes the total, the counters and the percent words and clears the flag.

evidence: Accepts only while j1939_standby_flag == STANDING_BY (1) (else DIAG_NACK_NOT_READY); then j1939_standby_flag = SESSION_ACTIVE (0), diagnostic_session_state = ACTIVE (1) and cal_write_mode = 0xee, DIAG_ACK. The rows are e2m 1328 +0 Development_Mode, 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable and 0010 +0 RUN_LOC; 0 / 1 / 0xee is also the start-up (cal_write_mode = 0xee in the boot list), power-down (cm848_runPowerDownSequence) and dump state, so this LEAVES development mode and turns the RAM refresh on. Registered as J1939 diagnostic service 7 (cm848_registerJ1939DiagnosticHandlers). The owner's review note is kept at the end of the plate; the main session shows the rename to the owner.
plate_comment: Leaves development mode and turns the RAM refresh back on (J1939 diagnostic service 7): accepted only while j1939_standby_flag is STANDING_BY (e2m 1328 +0 Development_Mode = 1), otherwise it returns DIAG_NACK_NOT_READY. Then it sets j1939_standby_flag = SESSION_ACTIVE (development mode 0), diagnostic_session_state = ACTIVE (e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable = 1) and cal_write_mode = 0xee (e2m 0010 +0 RUN_LOC; 0xee is also the start-up value) and returns DIAG_ACK. There is no engine state check; the force variant (service 22, 0x21694) requires the engine to be stopped but not development mode. | jlaustill reviewed - hopefully accurate

evidence: Stores diagnostic_session_state = INACTIVE (RAM_Refresh_Enable 0), j1939_standby_flag = STANDING_BY (Development_Mode 1) and cal_write_mode = 0xea (RUN_LOC), returns DIAG_ACK: the opposite of the boot / power-down / dump state, so it ENTERS development mode. Called as diagnostic service 10 and by cm848_processPciDiagnosticRequest right after pci_security_unlocked_flag = 1 (the security key was accepted). With the refresh disabled cm848_onEepromBlockRead stops reloading the mirror, j1939_writeDiagMemory writes EEPROM addresses only to the RAM mirror (its queue branch needs diagnostic_session_state == ACTIVE) and cm848_lookupApplicationMemoryRegionType gives the register ranges type 3 instead of 10 (table 0x53a33a, STANDING_BY column). The owner's review note is kept at the end of the plate; the main session shows the rename to the owner.
plate_comment: Enters development mode (J1939 diagnostic service 10, also called by cm848_processPciDiagnosticRequest right after the PCI security key has been accepted): disables the RAM refresh (diagnostic_session_state = INACTIVE, e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable = 0), sets j1939_standby_flag = STANDING_BY (e2m 1328 +0 Development_Mode = 1) and cal_write_mode = 0xea (e2m 0010 +0 RUN_LOC), and returns DIAG_ACK. With the refresh off, RAM calibration edits are not overwritten (the refresh pass and the periodic EEPROM mirror reload, cm848_onEepromBlockRead, stop), diagnostic writes to EEPROM addresses and EEPROM parameter ID writes go to the RAM mirror only (cm848_lookupParameterIdAddress, j1939_writeDiagMemory), and the two register address ranges of the diagnostic memory services open (cm848_lookupApplicationMemoryRegionType). The way back is service 7 (0x21624) or, with the engine stopped, service 22 (0x21694). | jlaustill review 2026-05-25 - hopefully accurate

evidence: Refuses with DIAG_NACK_PROTECTED while not_safe_to_program_flag == 1 (engine_state != STOPPED, 0x2bf44); otherwise it always stores diagnostic_session_state = ACTIVE (refresh on) and, only if cal_write_mode == 0xea (development), cal_write_mode = 0xee and j1939_standby_flag = SESSION_ACTIVE, so it LEAVES development mode without requiring it (service 7 requires it); the only unconditional store is the refresh enable, so cm848_forceEnableRamRefresh is the alternative name if the owner prefers that half. Registered as diagnostic service 22 (0x16). The owner's note is about != 1 and == 0xea / 0xee not rendering as enums: cal_write_mode is e2m 0010 +0 RUN_LOC (0xee normal / 0xea development here) and not_safe_to_program_flag is e2m 000D SAFE2PRG, both enum candidates. The note is kept at the end of the plate; the main session shows the rename to the owner.
plate_comment: Forces an exit from development mode when it is safe to program (J1939 diagnostic service 22): with not_safe_to_program_flag clear (engine stopped) it always turns the RAM refresh on (diagnostic_session_state = ACTIVE, e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable = 1) and, only if cal_write_mode is 0xea (development mode), also restores cal_write_mode = 0xee and j1939_standby_flag = SESSION_ACTIVE (e2m 1328 +0 Development_Mode = 0); it returns DIAG_ACK. With the engine not stopped it returns DIAG_NACK_PROTECTED and changes nothing. Unlike service 7 (0x21624) it does not require development mode to be on. | jlaustill reviewed 2026-05-25 - frustrated about != 1 and == 0xea/0xee not working as enums

evidence: Writes the one 12-byte block descriptor at 0x3fd2c4 (RAM start sensor_channel_cal_block_start, RAM end sensor_channel_ram_start, source ROM 0x64aea), points the cursor 0x3fd2d0 at it, restarts sensor_cal_ram_write_ptr / sensor_cal_rom_read_ptr, clears sensor_cal_write_dirty_flag and sets diagnostic_session_state = ACTIVE (e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable), sensor_validation_result = 1 (10C7 +2 Powerdown_Refresh_Enable) and sensor_cal_session_state_prev = 1. Its only caller, the refresh pass cm848_initProtectionModule, calls it when sensor_cal_session_state_prev == 0 and diagnostic_session_state != INACTIVE, i.e. on the first pass and when the refresh is enabled again.
plate_comment: RAM refresh initializer: fills the one block descriptor of the refresh table (12-byte entries at 0x3fd2c4: RAM start sensor_channel_cal_block_start 0x3feed0, RAM end sensor_channel_ram_start 0x40a046, source ROM 0x64aea), points the current-descriptor cursor at 0x3fd2d0 at it, restarts the compare cursors (sensor_cal_ram_write_ptr = the RAM start, sensor_cal_rom_read_ptr = the ROM source), clears sensor_cal_write_dirty_flag, sets diagnostic_session_state = ACTIVE (e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable = 1), sensor_validation_result = 1 (e2m 10C7 +2 Powerdown_Refresh_Enable) and sensor_cal_session_state_prev = 1. Called only by cm848_initProtectionModule (the refresh pass) on its first pass and whenever the refresh has just been enabled again (sensor_cal_session_state_prev = 0 while diagnostic_session_state is not INACTIVE).

evidence: Called in a loop, do { cm848_initProtectionModule(...); } while (power_down_start_flag == 0), by cm848_applicationMain and cm848_restartApplicationWithoutReset, so each call is one background pass. While diagnostic_session_state != INACTIVE (e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable) it compares up to 100 bytes (50 words) per call between sensor_cal_ram_write_ptr and sensor_cal_rom_read_ptr and rewrites each differing RAM word (the quote), setting sensor_cal_write_dirty_flag. At the end of a cycle it sets mask 1 of fault_detected_bits_0_to_15 if anything was rewritten, else clears it (e2m 1036 +0 RAM_Image_Word_Error 'RAM refresh generated error'; fault 0 -> ROM slot table 0x5985a -> obd_dtc_code_table = P0606). The block is 0x3feed0-0x40a046 against ROM 0x64aea (a flash parameter block; the EEPROM mirror ends at 0x3feec1). The e2m text 'COMPARE RAM TO EEPROM' fits the other half of the refresh: cm848_periodicTaskSet_protection2 -> cm848_startEepromBlockRead re-reads the EEPROM 30 words at a time and cm848_onEepromBlockRead copies them into the mirror only while diagnostic_session_state != INACTIVE.
plate_comment: RAM refresh pass - the body of the background loop of cm848_applicationMain and cm848_restartApplicationWithoutReset (do { ... } while (power_down_start_flag == 0)). While diagnostic_session_state is not INACTIVE (e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable = 1) each call compares up to 100 bytes (50 words) of the current block of the refresh table with its source and rewrites every RAM word that differs (sensor_cal_write_dirty_flag = 1). The one block is the sensor channel calibration block (sensor_channel_cal_block_start .. sensor_channel_ram_start, 0x3feed0-0x40a046) against ROM 0x64aea (the EEPROM mirror ends before it, at 0x3feec1); the EEPROM side of the refresh is the periodic mirror reload (cm848_periodicTaskSet_protection2 -> cm848_startEepromBlockRead, 30 words per read, copied in by cm848_onEepromBlockRead only while diagnostic_session_state is not INACTIVE). When a cycle through all blocks ends it sets fault bit 0 (fault_detected_bits_0_to_15 |= 1, e2m 1036 +0 RAM_Image_Word_Error 'RAM refresh generated error'; fault 0 -> ROM slot table 0x5985a -> obd_dtc_code_table = P0606) if any word was rewritten during the cycle, else clears it; it counts cycles in sensor_cal_ring_cycle_count. It calls uds_session_state_init when the refresh has just been enabled (sensor_cal_session_state_prev = 0) and clears fault bit 0 on that edge. It does nothing while the refresh is disabled (development mode).

members.comment: RAM refresh off (development mode); the refresh pass and the EEPROM mirror reload do nothing; stored by the reset service and temporarily by cm848_runCylinderContributionTest
RAM refresh on (the normal state); stored at start-up and power-down and by the activate services
Remove; nothing stores or tests 2 and the e2m record has no value labels

comment: e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable '[RREN] ENABLES COMPARE RAM TO EEPROM ALGORITHM' (HEX, word; 1 in the dump; address from the ECU's parameter ID table). 1 = RAM refresh enabled (the start-up and normal state), 0 = disabled (development mode). While enabled: the refresh pass cm848_initProtectionModule (the background loop of cm848_applicationMain) compares the sensor channel calibration block 0x3feed0-0x40a046 with ROM 0x64aea and rewrites differing words (setting fault 0 = P0606, e2m 1036 +0 RAM_Image_Word_Error, when it had to), the periodic EEPROM block read (cm848_periodicTaskSet_protection2 -> cm848_startEepromBlockRead) is copied into the RAM mirror by cm848_onEepromBlockRead, and j1939_writeDiagMemory refuses RAM writes into 0x3fd480-0x40a046 and queues EEPROM-address writes to the EEPROM. Stored 1 at start-up (cm848_initEepromDriverAndLoadMirror), by cm848_runPowerDownSequence, uds_session_state_init and the activate services; stored 0 by the reset service and, while it edits calibration words, by cm848_runCylinderContributionTest (1 again after). The supervisor chip register 46 read and the periodic supervisor configuration rewrite run only while it is 0. main_loop's psVar4 < &diagnostic_session_state is a loop-end address, not a use.
evidence: Stores: 0 (INACTIVE) in the reset service and at the start of cm848_runCylinderContributionTest; 1 (ACTIVE) in cm848_initEepromDriverAndLoadMirror, the activate and force-activate services, cm848_runPowerDownSequence, uds_session_state_init and the end of the cylinder test; every compare is == INACTIVE, != INACTIVE or == ACTIVE and nothing stores or tests 2. e2m 10C7 +0 RAM_Refresh_Enable resolves here through the parameter ID table; dump (word) 1. Enabled: the refresh pass cm848_initProtectionModule runs, cm848_onEepromBlockRead copies the block into the mirror only under if (diagnostic_session_state != INACTIVE) (the periodic read: cm848_periodicTaskSet_protection2 -> cm848_startEepromBlockRead), j1939_writeDiagMemory refuses RAM writes into the protected window; the supervisor register 46 read and configuration rewrite need == INACTIVE. e2m fit: RREN 'ENABLES COMPARE RAM TO EEPROM ALGORITHM' is that EEPROM mirror reload; the other half is the flash block loop cm848_initProtectionModule (RAM 0x3feed0-0x40a046 against ROM 0x64aea, after the mirror end 0x3feec1), whose e2m record is 10C7 +2 Powerdown_Refresh_Enable (sensor_validation_result, set to 1 by uds_session_state_init, cleared by a successful cm848_commitEepromMirrorToEeprom and read by nothing in the decompile). main_loop's psVar4 < &diagnostic_session_state is a loop-end address, not a use. A plain word flag would do (nothing differs from 0 / 1); the two-member enum keeps the compares readable.

members.comment: Normal operation; stored by the activate services and the power-down sequence; the register address ranges of the diagnostic memory services are refused
Development mode; stored only by the reset service together with the RAM refresh disabled; the activate service needs it and the register address ranges of the diagnostic memory services open

comment: e2m 1328 +0 Development_Mode '[SSDVMD] RAM Refresh disabled mode indicated by config name RUN_LOC = AAh' (UNITLESS, word; 0 in the dump; address from the ECU's parameter ID table). 1 = development mode: set by the reset service (also after a PCI security key is accepted) together with diagnostic_session_state INACTIVE (RAM refresh disabled) and cal_write_mode (e2m 0010 +0 RUN_LOC) = 0xea - this build uses 0xea, not the 0xaa of the e2m text; 0 = normal: stored by the activate service, by the force-activate service (only when cal_write_mode was 0xea) and by cm848_runPowerDownSequence. Tested == STANDING_BY only: the activate service accepts only while it is 1 (else DIAG_NACK_NOT_READY), and cm848_lookupApplicationMemoryRegionType gives the register ranges 0x2fc000-0x301fff and 0x303800-0x307fff type 3 (accessible) while it is 1 and type 10 (refused) otherwise (table 0x53a33a). No J1939 broadcast is gated by it.
evidence: Stores: 1 (STANDING_BY) only in the reset service, together with the refresh disabled and cal_write_mode = 0xea; 0 (SESSION_ACTIVE) in the activate service, in the force-activate service (only when cal_write_mode == 0xea) and in cm848_runPowerDownSequence; compares: the activate gate == STANDING_BY and cm848_lookupApplicationMemoryRegionType == STANDING_BY. The flash2 table at 0x53a33a (dumped) has type 3 for the register ranges 0x2fc000-0x301fff and 0x303800-0x307fff in the STANDING_BY column and 10 in the other, all other regions identical in both: an independent sign that 1 is the development state. Dump (word) 0; e2m 1328 +0 Development_Mode resolves here through the parameter ID table. e2m mismatch: it says RUN_LOC = AAh, this build writes 0xea. No J1939 broadcast depends on it, so the old 'J1939 broadcasts suppressed' / 'standing by' wording has no basis in the code. A plain word flag would do.
